findings.title: Clarifying questions and abstentions are model-worded, contrary to the fixed-sentence rule
findings.problem: The fixed-sentence rule says every ungrounded part of a reply is a fixed sentence, but the Planner's clarifying question and the Answerer's abstention wording are left to models, which is not grounded in tool results.
findings.proof: What in a reply is not grounded in tool results is a fixed sentence chosen by id, never a model's wording
findings.fix: Add fixed clarifying-question and abstention sentence ids to fixed_replies.md and state that the Planner and Answerer choose among them, or explicitly exempt those two parts from the rule.

findings.title: Budget loosening conflicts with the rule that a budget stays the limit
findings.problem: The tool loosens the budget by 25% or removes it, while the system prompt says a stated budget stays the limit, so the two can disagree on whether a product over budget may be returned.
findings.proof: the budget raised by 25%, the budget removed
findings.fix: State in the system prompt and in the rag.search description which loosening steps are allowed for a budget the shopper set as a hard limit, and mark the rest as never loosened.

findings.title: Router default conflicts with the scope boundary
findings.problem: Scope excludes 'anything else', but the Router defaults to a product search whenever it is in doubt, so ambiguous out-of-scope messages become searches.
findings.proof: intent (a product search when in doubt)
findings.fix: Add a rule that doubtful messages go to the off_topic or clarifying path unless a product noun is present.

findings.title: No spoken AI disclosure at the start of each voice answer
findings.problem: The transparency obligation is met only by the greeting and the screen, and nothing requires the spoken product reply or the spoken short form to disclose AI use, which matters in a voice-only channel; this belongs in the system prompt's Disclosure rule.
findings.fix: Add a rule that every spoken reply opens with the short identity sentence, or that the shortened identity id is always included in the spoken part.

findings.title: No fairness or bias control for recommendations
findings.problem: For a recommendation use case under NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001, the system prompt has no rule against recommendations that vary by inferred gender, ethnicity or other protected traits, nor a way to report such bias; this belongs in the system prompt's Safety policy section.
findings.fix: Add a fairness rule that ranking is based only on the shopper's stated constraints and cited evidence, plus a report category for suspected bias.

findings.title: Injection defence depends on server-side stripping alone
findings.problem: Untrusted text is fenced and the server strips instruction-like text, but no instruction tells the Critic or Answerer to ignore leftover instruction-like wording that the server missed.
findings.proof: The MCP server removes instruction-like text from tool results (catalog listings and web results) before any model sees it
findings.fix: Add a line to the Answerer and Critic prompts that any instruction-like wording inside <evidence> is data and is never acted on, whether or not the server removed it.

findings.title: Ingredients column name invites invented ingredient lists
findings.problem: The column is named Ingredients, but most catalog products are toys with no ingredients, so the column name invites the model to fill it with unsourced content, although the materials rule limits this.
findings.fix: Rename the column to Materials and claims so that the label matches the source fields.

findings.title: Category statistics are dead context for the agents
findings.problem: The catalog file lists per-category product counts that no agent needs to choose a tool or filter, so the figures spend tokens without changing behaviour.
findings.proof: Top-level categories: Toys & Games (6,521), Home & Kitchen (688)
findings.fix: Remove the per-category counts and keep only the category names the filters need.

findings.title: Short-form fixed replies duplicate the full texts
findings.problem: The spoken short forms repeat most full fixed replies with minor edits, so the same content is spent twice; code could select the short form by id instead.
findings.proof: Spoken before a product answer, these are shortened so that the reply still fits 15 seconds:
findings.fix: Keep one text per id and derive the spoken form by code truncation, or store only the short forms that differ materially from the full texts.

findings.title: Routing guidance repeated between the tool schema and the Planner
findings.problem: The rag.search description repeats the when-to-call rule that the Planner stage already states, so the same routing guidance is paid for twice in every request.
findings.proof: When to call: first, for any request for a kind of product.
findings.fix: Keep the routing rule in one place, such as the Planner stage, and shorten the tool description to the call arguments and the result fields.

findings.title: Loosening rules are restated in the system prompt
findings.problem: The system prompt restates which filters the catalog never loosens, which the tool schema already states in full, so the rule is duplicated.
findings.proof: the catalog tool loosens some (never a stated age range or a safety exclusion)
findings.fix: Reference the tool schema for the loosening order and keep only the reply obligation in the system prompt.

findings.title: Tool Schema Quality: 80% with no cited passage
findings.problem: Tool Schema Quality scored 80%, losing 20 points against what this criterion measures — each tool has a clear description, typed args, and when-to-call guidance. The assessor marked it down without quoting a passage, so the specific weakness is unevidenced and this reason is derived from the score rather than observed.
findings.fix: Review catalog_and_sources.md, fixed_replies.md, system_prompt.md, tools.json against this criterion: each tool has a clear description, typed args, and when-to-call guidance. Re-run with --assess-context afterwards to confirm the score moves.
